fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Entry Area; Walkway; Landscaped Area; Open Lawn Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Limited Turnaround Space; Dense Vegetation
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the street-facing driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach the front of the residence without obstruction.
• Mark a designated turnaround area near the residence so drivers of large emergency vehicles can reverse or reposition without damaging the lawn or landscaping.
• Trim vegetation along the driveway edges so mirrors and equipment on larger emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Cut back dense plantings near the front entry so responders carrying equipment can move from the driveway to the front door without being slowed or blocked.
• Keep the front walkway clear of potted plants, decorative items, or other objects that could block a stretcher or equipment movement to the door.
• Thin dense vegetation near the residence to create open space between plant masses and the structure so responders can move around the exterior of the home.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Scattered Shrubs; Vegetation Near Structure; Open Green Space; Irrigated Landscape; Limited Vegetation Separation; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Vegetation Along Driveway
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang directly over or touch the roof and eaves.
• Thin shrubs growing close to the exterior walls of the house to create open space between the plants and the structure.
• Remove or thin shrubs and low tree branches along the driveway to keep the travel path clear on both sides.
• Separate clusters of shrubs near the house so individual plants are not touching each other.
• Keep low-hanging branches on scattered trees trimmed up from the ground to reduce the path fire can take from ground level into the tree canopy.
• Clear any dead leaves, dry plant debris, and loose mulch that has built up directly against the foundation or exterior walls.
• Maintain the irrigated landscape areas immediately around the house to keep ground cover low and moist during dry periods.
• Move any firewood, lumber, or stored materials away from the exterior walls of the house and any outbuildings.
